tldr: AP2 defines signed mandates that prove what a user approved an agent to buy. Version 0.2 has Checkout and Payment Mandates, each closed (exact values) or open (constraints), carried inside a commerce protocol such as UCP.
whyItExists: When an agent pays, the merchant, the card issuer and the network cannot tell whether the person behind it agreed to this purchase. Today's payment systems assume a human clicked buy. AP2 gives every party a signed, checkable record of what the user approved: either the exact checkout and amount, or a set of limits (merchants, items, price range, budget, dates) inside which the agent may close a purchase on its own. The record later serves as evidence in a dispute.

whatItIsNot.text: Not a payment rail. AP2 moves no money; it carries authorization evidence on top of cards, bank transfers or stablecoins.
Not A2A. A2A is one transport that the samples use; v0.2 treats AP2 as a security feature inside a commerce protocol.
Not a Google-only project any more. Google donated it to the FIDO Alliance on 2026-04-28, and specification work now sits with FIDO working groups.
Not the three mandates of 2025. Version 0.2 has no Intent Mandate and no Cart Mandate, only Checkout and Payment Mandates.
Not proven in production. No primary source shows live use of AP2 mandates, inside UCP or anywhere else.
Not the Machine Payments Protocol from Stripe and Tempo, and not Visa's TAP. In AP2, MPP is the Merchant Payment Processor role, and Trusted Agent Provider is a delegation model.
Not built on W3C VC 2.0 or DIDs. v0.2 uses SD-JWT VC, OpenID4VP and the Digital Credentials API; VC 2.0 and DIDs are only the wider family.

changedRecently.text: The Delegate SD-JWT draft that chains AP2 mandates was posted to the IETF as an individual draft.
v0.2 released with open and closed Checkout and Payment Mandates; the same day Google donated AP2 to the FIDO Alliance.
Last commit on the AP2 main branch; 65 pull requests opened since then (to 2026-10-21), none merged.
Google said it would begin bringing AP2 to Google products in the coming months, starting with Gemini Spark.
On issue 268 a specification author wrote that further iterations had officially moved to FIDO.
arXiv:2608.23858 cataloged 48 threats to AP2 v0.2, eight of them in the High band.
UCP renamed its AP2 extension dev.ucp.common.payment.ap2_mandate and aligned it with AP2 v0.2.
A third-party Internet-Draft binding delivery evidence to AP2 mandates reached -01; its abstract still names v0.1 objects.
FIDO's Payments Technical Working Group presented targets: harmonized AP2 and Verifiable Intent specifications by the end of 2026 and a first consolidated version in mid-2027.
